findings.title: Dataclass default `queued=timezone.now()` is evaluated once at class definition
findings.body: In `AssignmentSource`, the field `queued: datetime = timezone.now()` is a classic Python dataclass pitfall: the default expression is evaluated once when the decorator runs, not per instance. Every `AssignmentSource` constructed without an explicit `queued` argument will share the same timestamp (the time the module was first imported). It should be `queued: datetime = field(default_factory=timezone.now)` (with `field` imported from `dataclasses`). The field is currently unused in the sync logic so the impact is low, but it is incorrect and will surprise anyone who later relies on `queued` for ordering, TTL, or debugging.

findings.title: `from_dict` silently swallows all errors and returns None
findings.body: `AssignmentSource.from_dict` uses a bare `except (ValueError, TypeError)` and returns `None` for any malformed payload. This is unsafe because the only signal callers get is `None`, which is treated identically to "no assignment source was provided", meaning `should_sync` will happily allow the outbound sync to proceed. Concrete risks: (a) forward-compatibility — if a new required field is added to `AssignmentSource` later, every in-flight Celery task whose `assignment_source_dict` predates the change will silently deserialize to `None`, re-enabling the very sync cycle this PR is trying to fix; (b) corruption of task payloads will be invisible. The method should at minimum log the malformed payload, or raise so the caller can decide (e.g., retry vs. drop) instead of silently dropping the cycle-prevention signal.

findings.title: `sync_status_outbound` abstract signature adds `assignment_source` that is never passed anywhere
findings.body: The abstract method `sync_status_outbound` is updated to take `assignment_source: AssignmentSource | None = None`, but no caller in this PR (or visible in the diff) ever passes it. The `sync_assignee_outbound` task only invokes `sync_assignee_outbound`, not `sync_status_outbound`. This is misleading: the PR description claims to break "issue sync cycles" (plural) and the new signature implies status sync cycles are being addressed, but the status cycle is not actually broken — inbound `sync_status_inbound` still triggers `sync_status_outbound` without any source guard. Any concrete implementation that does not already accept `**kwargs` will also break if a future caller does pass `assignment_source`. Either remove the parameter from the abstract signature until the status-side fix is implemented, or implement and thread the assignment_source through the status path so the cycle is actually closed.

findings.title: Typo in test method name: `test_from_dict_inalid_data`
findings.body: The test method `test_from_dict_inalid_data` contains a spelling error — "inalid" should be "invalid". This will surface in test reports and any test-runner output that uses the method name.
